agree.reason: The clear math, the June fallback that could bring ads back, and the plan to keep the ad sales lead in a new role give the two ad-background members solid ground to vote yes, but the $30,000 gap and the unfilled bridge-funding line will make them hesitate.

honest.reason: The memo treats full replacement as a target and states the first-year gap openly, but 'it shows the model works at our scale' rests on one secondhand example, and the claim that ads slow the site and hurt the reader relationship isn't in the brief.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the 36% drop, the 1.5% pilot conversion, the 875 members needed (about 6% of the list), the quarter already reached and a $50,000 year-one estimate, but it misses the strongest true comparison: the pilot signed about 35 people a week, while the target needs only about 13 a week.

right_comparison.reason: Staying with ads is shown as a declining line projected to about $65,000 next year and lower after that, so the board sees the trend rather than a flat $84,000.

qualification.reason: The June 30 checkpoint has a date, a threshold of 450 and a consequence (options, including bringing back ads), but the March and December checkpoints have no consequence if missed, and pilot retention is still a blank placeholder.

objections.reason: The memo answers what will happen to the 11-year staffer and offers a way back to ads, but it never says why ads have to end completely instead of running alongside membership, which is the question the sales-minded members are most likely to press.

fit.reason: It is a properly formatted memo that ends with a specific requested action and runs about one page, though it is tight against that limit.
